analysis.one_liner: "Makes it a federal crime for former members of Congress to lobby Congress or executive officials."
analysis.headline: "The bill to ban former members of Congress from lobbying never got a committee hearing or a vote before the Congress ended."
analysis.plain_summary: "The bill would amend federal criminal law so that any former senator or representative who makes a lobbying contact with executive branch officials or members of Congress could be prosecuted, with penalties under section 216 of title 18."
analysis.who_benefits: "Ordinary Americans, who currently pay for lobbying access through favorable treatment of industries and wealthy interests; the bill aims to reduce the advantage of former legislators who sell their connections."
analysis.who_pays: "Former members of Congress, who would lose a lucrative career path, and the lobbying firms and industries that hire them for their access."

drawbacks.text: "A lifetime lobbying ban is unusually severe; critics argue it may deter qualified people from serving and could face legal challenges on First Amendment grounds."
"The bill never received a hearing or markup, so its practical design, enforcement, and scope were never examined by the committee."

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: "A potentially meaningful anti-corruption measure, but with real concerns about severity and constitutionality that were never debated; as written, it may be blunt."

outcome.mechanism: "The House referred the bill to the Judiciary Committee, which never scheduled a hearing or a vote before the Congress ended."

narrative.text: "The bill was introduced on April 30, 2024 and referred to the House Judiciary Committee the same day."
"The bill had no committee action, no floor vote, and died at the end of the 118th Congress in January 2025."

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: "Lobbying firms, industries that hire former lawmakers, and former members of Congress who benefit from the current system, all of whom are better off because the bill never advanced."

for.name: Rep. Jared Golden
for.what_they_did: "Introduced the bill to criminalize lobbying by former members of Congress."

for.name: Cosponsor (1 Democrat)
for.what_they_did: "Added support as the bill's sole cosponsor."

against.name: House Judiciary Committee
against.what_they_did: "Received the referral but took no further action, never scheduling a hearing or vote."

sides.party_line_note: "The bill had two Democratic sponsors and never received any vote, so its partisan appeal was never tested."

industries.industry: Lobbying firms and government relations industry
industries.note: "The bill would shrink the pool of former legislators available for hire, reducing the access-for-hire advantage that lobbying firms sell to clients."
